title: Model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama/Mistral/Qwen quirks + GQA/MQA tuning
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Performance: reduced P50 latency and token-cost for Llama/Mistral/Qwen models via kernel selection, attention tiling, and GQA/MQA quantization tuning. Includes scheduler improvements for continuous batching and KV cache compaction. Safe rollout: canary on Dedicated then gradual Hosted rollout.
description:
Motivation: several model-specific quirks (rotary size in Llama, Mistral attention head packing, Qwen attention causal-offsets) and the recent adoption of grouped quantization (GQA/MQA) exposed suboptimal kernel selection and memory layouts in the serving runtime. This PR addresses kernel selection heuristics, attention tiling, and KV cache memory layout to recover latency and throughput for these models while keeping regression risk low.

Summary of changes: unified kernel selector heuristics to consider per-model rotary/hpos quirks, a new fused rotary+qkv kernel for Llama-like configs, attention tiling and causal-offset fixes for Qwen, improved Mistral-compatible flash-attention fallback path, GQA/MQA-aware packing/stride adjustments to avoid misaligned GEMM kernels, KV cache compaction for continuous batching to reduce memory fragmentation, and scheduler improvements that prioritize low-latency short requests and implement an early-flush policy for mixed workloads.

Benchmarks: internal perf-canary results (N=1000 runs, 8xA100, 512 context) show P50 token latency improvement of 18-32% across target models and average token-cost drop of 12% for GQA/MQA-quantized variants. Throughput (tokens/sec) improved by 10-22% depending on batch composition. See benchmark numbers in commits.

Backward compatibility & rollout: changes are behind a runtime flag (model_opt_v2) and opt-in per-model in the model catalog. Safe rollout plan: canary on Dedicated pool -> monitor per-route latency/cost -> gradual enable on Hosted. No API surface changes.

Testing: unit tests for kernel selection and quantization packing; integration tests in perf-canary with representative prompts; additional CI perf gating was added to catch regressions for Llama/Mistral/Qwen families.

Notes: some microbenchmarks showed small increases for very short token sequences (<8 tokens) in contrived setups; scheduler adjustable knobs (early_flush_threshold) allow tuning based on observed workload mix.
